clue.text: Margate's amazingly famous entertainer

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a startling way, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the town name with its possessive S gives eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer at the Kent seaside resort of Margate draws gasps.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the S of the possessive is part of the fodder: 'amazingly' rearranges all eight letters of MARGATES. Margate is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a hugely celebrated performer, far beyond an ordinary star.

clue.text: Yard gets detective to pursue gang? That's novel

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so these pieces come after the gang

parts.note: a mob is a gang of people
dick is slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard sends a detective after a criminal gang: what a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard but only gives its abbreviation. 'to pursue' puts Y and DICK after MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Moby-Dick is Herman Melville's famous novel about a white whale.

clue.text: Dramatist penning minor work is awkward

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a sheep pen, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: John Gay, author of The Beggar's Opera
WK is a short form of work, a minor version of the word

explanation.surface: A playwright writing a small piece is clumsy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, fitting the dramatist, but signals an enclosure. John Gay is the usual crossword dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky is a synonym for awkward and ungainly in manner or movement.

clue.text: Sailor carried skins far off

indicators.note: off means bad or gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman took animal pelts on a long journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CARRIED SKINS FAR, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan seaman who circumnavigated the globe.

clue.text: In reality, a source of danger, with resistance lowered

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the light

parts.note: a threat is a source of danger
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Truly, a risk lessens once opposition is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowered' works because this is a down entry: the resistance letter slides further down, giving the answer's second word.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in one's true nature, beneath appearances.

clue.text: Recall schoolboy's howler?

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a schoolboy is a pupil; with the possessive this gives pupil's

explanation.surface: Remembering a classroom blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring mistake, a blunder of the kind called a slip.

clue.text: Dancing showgirls seen to be less ambitious

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Chorus girls observed to scale back their dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower one's sights is an idiom for aiming lower, accepting a less ambitious goal.

clue.text: For every work, I'll support the French composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece goes below the others

parts.note: per means for each one
to work is to go, as a machine goes
les is French for the (plural)
I'll is I will, so the letter I

explanation.surface: Each piece of music will be backed by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' puts I below LES in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an eighteenth-century Italian composer of the Stabat Mater.

clue.text: Person who sends bill

definitions.meaning: a bill is a notice or advertisement stuck on a wall

explanation.definitionFit: One who mails things is someone who posts; a placard is also called this.

clue.text: A check on article about saint's holy writings

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to vet is to check
S is the abbreviation for saint
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Checking an item concerning a holy man's scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside VET, giving VEST; 'on' sets that above the article A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collection of sacred Zoroastrian scriptures.

clue.text: Telephone line cut in shady area

indicators.note: cut means a piece is removed

parts.note: blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: Phone wires severed in a tree-lined spot.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOWER is old British slang for a telephone; 'cut' removes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a leafy shelter or arbour, a shaded place in a garden.

clue.text: What lexicographers need to do, to define "quarrel'?

explanation.definitionFit: To have words is an idiom for arguing; dictionary compilers literally possess vocabulary.

clue.text: Idly imagines Dad's Army clashes with start of EastEnders

indicators.note: clashing parts collide and jumble, so the letters are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Musing about two TV programmes colliding in the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom and EastEnders a British soap. 'start of' gives E; 'clashes' rearranges DADSARMY with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreams as a verb means drifts into idle fantasies while awake.

clue.text: Royal Highness acquires single wine-producing area

parts.note: RH abbreviates Royal Highness
single means one

explanation.surface: A royal personage buys a lone vineyard region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone valley in France is a famous wine region.

clue.text: Piece of furniture I secure on back of vehicle

indicators.note: on the back of means following, so these pieces come after the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
to net is to secure or capture

explanation.surface: Fastening a cupboard onto the rear of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a cupboard with shelves or drawers, a piece of furniture.

clue.text: Loud demonstrator making endless din in pub, right?

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: endless means losing the last letter

parts.note: a racket is a din

explanation.surface: A rowdy protester is making a racket in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims RACKET to RACKE, which goes 'in' BAR, then R.
explanation.definitionFit: A barracker is someone who jeers noisily, a heckler.

clue.text: Warn them leaders are missing in battle

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their first letters, which are dropped

explanation.surface: Alerting troops that commanders have gone absent in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders are missing' drops W and T from WARN THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem was a 1944 Second World War battle in the Netherlands.

clue.text: One must be mad to 'take charge of investigation

parts.note: to head is to lead or take charge of
a case is an investigation by police

explanation.surface: Only a lunatic would lead this inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A headcase is slang for a crazy or unbalanced person.

clue.text: Sitting in judgement is hard

explanation.definitionFit: Trying means judging a case in court, and also exhausting or difficult.

clue.text: Plain-living person, mostly tactless and old

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: gauche means socially awkward or tactless

explanation.surface: A simple-living sort is rather clumsy and aged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain-living' reads as frugal, but means living on the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American cowboy of the pampas, the grassy plains.

clue.text: Trace undershirt — singlet that's oddly gone missing

parts.note: a vest is an undershirt

indicators.note: the odd letters have gone missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A hint of underwear when a top has strangely disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of SINGLET leaves IGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a small remaining sign or trace of something.

clue.text: Strive to grab place for entertainer?

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to vie is to strive or compete
a site is a place

explanation.surface: Fighting to secure a spot as a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: An entertainer here is a host, not a performer: the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitee is the person visited, who hosts or entertains the guests.

clue.text: Church overlooking a rented holiday property?

indicators.note: in a down entry, overlooking means placed above the next pieces

parts.note: let means rented out

explanation.surface: A rented holiday home sits above a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a cabin or holiday chalet often rented at resorts.

clue.text: Noisy crowd in store

indicators.note: noisy points to how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a horde is a crowd

explanation.surface: A loud mob in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy' signals a homophone: HORDE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile, a store of valuables or supplies.

clue.text: Incompetent naval leader in America gets overwhelmed

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: US is America

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: killed means overwhelmed, crushed or defeated

explanation.surface: A hopeless admiral in the USA meets defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes N from naval, which goes 'in' US.
explanation.definitionFit: Unskilled means lacking ability or training, hence incompetent.

clue.text: Animal secured by length of cut rope

indicators.note: secured by means held between the pieces
cut means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: an ass is an animal

explanation.surface: A beast tethered with a piece of severed cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the F from the clue's own small word; 'secured by' wraps the length abbreviation and that remnant round the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used to catch cattle.

clue.text: Fancy a drop to drink straightaway?

parts.note: to fancy is to like
a shot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Wanting a quick nip right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for immediately and eagerly.

clue.text: Book' house near the Mediterranean, perhaps

parts.note: the Mediterranean is an example of a sea

explanation.surface: A book about a home beside the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament, one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Part of the Christmas meal is a complete failure

explanation.definitionFit: The festive roast bird shares its name with slang for a flop.

clue.text: Kop supporter?

parts.note: looks like a Liverpool fan on the Kop stand, but read as the central stone that supports an arch, linked to the silent-film police

explanation.definitionFit: Keystone Kops were silent-film police; a keystone supports an arch.
